summary: This is a docs-only spot-check task: it registers a claim in ai-os/boss/ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml per protocol, adds a new verification note (ai-os/PREVIEW_DEPLOYMENT_SPOTCHECK_2026-07-26.md) documenting a live pass/fail check of the current most-recent open PR's Vercel preview deployment, and rewrites PROGRESS.md to reflect this task (the prior task's narrative is fully replaced, consistent with this repo's existing per-task PROGRESS.md convention seen in earlier commits, not an accidental content loss). No application code, schema, auth, CI workflow, or migration files are touched, so tier1 classification is appropriate despite PROGRESS.md's diff numerically brushing the heavy-deletion threshold in isolation (52 deleted/24 added) -- the deletions are the prior task's already-preserved-elsewhere narrative being swapped for this task's own, not a loss of load-bearing content, and the overall diff is dominated by net-new additive documentation (106 insertions vs 52 deletions across the whole changeset). I independently verified via `gh pr view 571` that the PR referenced in the note (headRefName worker/task-20260726-154345-phase-2-guardrail-coverage-expansion, createdAt 2026-07-26T16:03:12Z) is real and matches the note's claims exactly, giving confidence the reported spot-check work is genuine rather than fabricated. The note is honest about scope: it discloses the anonymous browser-render check was blocked by Vercel team SSO Deployment Protection and clearly separates that from the deploy-health verification it could perform (readyState READY, full route build, CI's own Vercel check green), which is the right way to report a partial verification rather than overclaiming.
